description: A FORM WITH THREE RED MESSAGES UNDER THREE FIELDS LOOKS CORRECT TO EVERYONE WHO CAN SEE IT. That is the illusion: being NEAR a field is not being attached to it, and assistive technology reads the attachment. Somebody filling the form by ear is told «Email» and nothing else, while «Enter a valid email address» sits in red an inch below, invisible to them. Nobody can check this by looking, which is why it survives in shipped products for years. This reads the wire out of the tree — aria-errormessage, aria-describedby, label — and reports: which messages are attached to which fields, which messages are attached to NOTHING, and which fields are marked invalid with no reason given at all. Pass `draw` to get the picture: a line from every field to its message, and a stub on every message whose line ends in mid-air. It deliberately under-reports: a message inside its field's label, and an error summary that links to its fields, are both correct by another route and are not called orphans. A wrongly accused form costs somebody an afternoon proving the tool wrong.

draw.description: Write a PNG here with the wiring drawn on the page: green lines for attached messages, red stubs for orphans
